posts.raw_content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kvEypYGj2D8

Probably the least surprising thing is that mud sharking is the superhighway into the sex industry. You've suddenly got a kid, you're already semi-degenerated and you're economically vulnerable.

The most surprising thing is that 'high class' is just marketing bs aimed at the buyer. Everyone expects a $20-100 street walker to have a pimp and be controlled by violence. But the girls who cost $300-500, who are well coiffed and wear designer clothes and are found in high end casinos and advertised escort services are no different. The marketing fiction is that they are high class, that they keep their money, they often claim that they're doing it to pay for their 'education', but it's all a lie. Part of it is toenhance their value, but more importantly it's a fig leaf for the upper middle class buyers who can afford those rates, so they can tell themselves they're engaging in a market transaction instead of human slavery.

It's easy to put these girls down for their choices, but when you hear their stories, hear how they were manipulated into a position of vulnerability, then coerced and finally terrorized, you can only feel sorry for them. 

The movie reinforces my visceral hatred of Vegas and the way black culture celebrates pimping. I kept thinking that if that were my daughter, the pimp would be hanging from a tree.

The good news is that the girls telling the stories all got out. Mostly when their pimps went to prison. They all found God. They all made something positive out of their experiences, by organizing against human trafficking. They seem to have found normal lives.

One, 'Bekah', was pardoned by President Trump in 2020. 

I encourage everyone to give it a watch.
